meta.title: FAQ - Prettier Config
meta.description: Answers to common questions about Prettier, .prettierrc files, and how to use the Prettier Config Generator.

hero.title: Frequently Asked Questions
hero.description: Everything you need to know about Prettier and this configuration generator.

items.question: What is Prettier Config Generator?
items.answer: Prettier Config Generator is a free, interactive web tool that lets you visually configure every Prettier option and instantly copy the resulting .prettierrc file. No manual editing required.

items.question: What is Prettier and why should I use it?
items.answer: Prettier is an opinionated code formatter that enforces a consistent style across your codebase. It removes all original styling and re-prints your code with a uniform format, eliminating style debates in code reviews.

items.question: What is a .prettierrc file?
items.answer: A .prettierrc file is a configuration file placed at the root of your project that tells Prettier how to format your code. It controls options like indentation, quote style, and line width.

items.question: How do I use this tool to generate my config?
items.answer: Select the Prettier options you want on the main page. Your configuration updates in real-time in the sidebar. Click "Copy Config" to copy the JSON to your clipboard, then paste it into a .prettierrc file at the root of your project.

items.question: Is Prettier Config Generator free?
items.answer: Yes, completely free. There is no signup, no account required, and no usage limits. The tool is also open source on GitHub.

items.question: Does this tool cover all Prettier options?
items.answer: Yes. This tool includes every officially supported Prettier option, with descriptions and default values shown for each one so you can make informed choices.

items.question: How do I copy and use the generated config?
items.answer: Click the "Copy Config" button in the sidebar on desktop, or tap the floating action button on mobile. Paste the copied JSON content into a new file named .prettierrc at the root of your project directory.

items.question: What is the difference between .prettierrc, prettier.config.js, and the prettier key in package.json?
items.answer: All three are valid ways to configure Prettier. .prettierrc supports JSON or YAML. prettier.config.js is a JavaScript module and allows dynamic configuration. The prettier key in package.json keeps everything in one file. The functionality is identical — it is a matter of preference.

items.question: Does Prettier work with TypeScript, React, and Vue?
items.answer: Yes. Prettier has built-in support for TypeScript, JSX/TSX (React), Vue single-file components, and many other formats. You may need to install additional plugins for some frameworks.

items.question: How do I integrate Prettier with VS Code?
items.answer: Install the "Prettier - Code formatter" extension from the VS Code marketplace. Then add "editor.defaultFormatter": "esbenp.prettier-vscode" and "editor.formatOnSave": true to your VS Code settings.

items.question: How do I run Prettier on my entire project?
items.answer: Run npx prettier --write . in your project root. This formats all supported files. Add prettier as a dev dependency with npm install --save-dev prettier for consistent results across your team.

items.question: What languages and file types does Prettier support?
items.answer: Prettier supports JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, TSX, CSS, SCSS, Less, HTML, Vue, Angular, JSON, YAML, Markdown, and more. It can also be extended with plugins for additional languages.

items.question: How do I ignore files from Prettier formatting?
items.answer: Create a .prettierignore file in your project root, using the same syntax as .gitignore. Files and directories listed there will be skipped by Prettier.

items.question: Can I use Prettier together with ESLint?
items.answer: Yes. Install eslint-config-prettier to disable ESLint formatting rules that conflict with Prettier. Run Prettier for formatting and ESLint for code quality rules — they complement each other perfectly.

items.question: What does the printWidth option do?
items.answer: printWidth tells Prettier the line length it should try to fit code within. It defaults to 80. This is a soft target — Prettier will exceed it if breaking the line would make the code less readable.

items.question: What is the difference between singleQuote and jsxSingleQuote?
items.answer: singleQuote controls whether Prettier uses single quotes in JavaScript/TypeScript strings. jsxSingleQuote specifically controls JSX attribute strings. You can set them independently.

items.question: How do I use the search feature on this site?
items.answer: Use the search bar at the top of the page to filter Prettier options by name, description, or keyword. Results update instantly as you type.

items.question: Does this site support dark mode?
items.answer: Yes. Click the theme toggle button in the header to switch between light mode, dark mode, and system preference. Your choice is saved automatically.

items.question: What is the default Prettier configuration?
items.answer: Prettier defaults include: printWidth: 80, tabWidth: 2, useTabs: false, semi: true, singleQuote: false, trailingComma: "all", bracketSpacing: true, and arrowParens: "always".

items.question: How do I report a bug or contribute to this project?
items.answer: Open an issue or pull request on the GitHub repository. The project welcomes contributions of all kinds, including new features, bug fixes, and translation improvements.

items.question: Which Prettier versions does this tool support?
items.answer: You can pick any Prettier 3.x release from the version dropdown — 3.0 through 3.6 plus "latest". The selected version's bundle is loaded on demand from jsDelivr, so the options list always matches that release's actual schema.

items.question: Which languages can I format in the Your Code tab?
items.answer: TypeScript, JavaScript, Flow, CSS, SCSS, Less, HTML, Vue, Angular templates, JSON, JSON5, JSON with comments, Markdown, MDX, YAML, and GraphQL. The parser is auto-detected from the input, but you can override it with the dropdown.

items.question: How does the shareable URL work?
items.answer: Click the share button and the current Prettier version, selected options, code, and parser override are LZ-compressed into the URL hash, then copied to your clipboard. Opening that link restores the exact same configuration. Nothing is sent to a server — everything stays in the browser.

items.question: What does the token count next to the diff mean?
items.answer: It shows how many AI tokens your input and output would cost under the selected model. GPT-4o / GPT-4 / GPT-3.5 use the official BPE tokenizers for an exact count; Claude, Gemini, Llama, and Mistral use a character-based approximation prefixed with "~".

items.question: Does my work survive a page refresh?
items.answer: Yes. Your Prettier version, option selections, and split-view / tokenizer preferences are saved to localStorage, so a reload restores everything. A shareable URL hash takes precedence if one is present when you open the page.

items.question: Why does the format error strip appear sometimes?
items.answer: When Prettier's parser can't parse your input — usually because the chosen parser doesn't match the code (e.g. CSS picked but you pasted JSX) — the error message appears in a red strip above the diff. Switch the parser to match your code and the error clears.

items.question: Can I preview my config against languages other than JavaScript?
items.answer: Yes. The Preview tab has its own parser dropdown next to the diff toggle, and each parser comes with a purpose-built sample — CSS, SCSS, Less, HTML, Vue, Angular, JSON / JSON5 / JSONC, Markdown, MDX, YAML, GraphQL, plus TypeScript / JS. Switching parsers re-formats the matching sample under your current options, so language-specific options like proseWrap, htmlWhitespaceSensitivity, and vueIndentScriptAndStyle have a place to demonstrate their effect. Your choice persists across reloads.

meta.title: Privacy Policy – Prettier Config
meta.description: How prettier-config.dev handles your data: your code never leaves your browser. Details on local storage, analytics, advertising cookies, and your choices.

hero.title: Privacy Policy
hero.description: This site is a client-side tool. Your code is formatted in your browser and is never uploaded to a server.

summary.title: The short version
items: The code you paste is formatted entirely inside your browser. It is never sent to, logged by, or stored on any server we control.
There are no accounts, no sign-ups, and no tracking profile is built from your code.
Your option choices are saved in your own browser's local storage so the page remembers them. You can clear them at any time.
We show ads through Google AdSense and measure aggregate traffic with Google Analytics. Both use cookies, and both are described in full below.

sections.title: Who is responsible
paragraphs: prettier-config.dev is an open-source project run by an individual developer, not a company. Throughout this policy, “we” and “the site” refer to that project.
If you have a question about anything here, the contact details are at the end of this page.

sections.title: Your code stays in your browser
paragraphs: The formatting engine is Prettier itself, loaded directly into your browser from a public CDN. When you paste code and see a formatted result, that work happens on your own machine — the text is never transmitted anywhere.

Share links work the same way. The configuration and code you share are compressed into the part of the URL after the “#” symbol, which browsers do not send to web servers. A share link is only readable by someone you choose to give it to.

sections.title: What is stored in your browser
paragraphs: The site keeps a few preferences in your browser's local storage so it can remember your setup between visits. This data stays on your device, is not a cookie, and is never transmitted to us.
items: prettier-config-state — your selected Prettier version, option choices, and enabled plugins.
prettier-config-diff-settings — whether you prefer the split or unified diff view, and your chosen token-counter model.
prettier-config-layout-v2 — the widths of the resizable editor panels.
theme — whether you chose the light, dark, or system appearance.
sections.footnote: You can remove all of it at any time by clearing site data for prettier-config.dev in your browser settings. Nothing breaks — the page simply returns to its defaults.

sections.title: Analytics
paragraphs: We use Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics to understand roughly how many people use the tool and which features get used. This is aggregate measurement: it tells us that an option was toggled, not who toggled it, and it never includes the code you paste.
Google may set cookies to do this. You can opt out across every site you visit by installing Google's Analytics opt-out browser add-on.

sections.title: Advertising
paragraphs: This site is free to use and is funded by advertising. We display ads through Google AdSense.
Google's use of advertising cookies enables it and its partners to serve ads to you based on your visit to this site and/or other sites on the Internet.

You can opt out of personalised advertising at any time through Google's Ads Settings. You can also opt out of some third-party vendors' use of cookies for personalised advertising via the industry opt-out page at aboutads.info.
Third-party vendors and ad networks other than Google may also serve ads on this site. Their use of cookies is governed by their own privacy policies, not this one.

sections.title: Consent in the EEA, the UK and Switzerland
paragraphs: If you visit from the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or Switzerland, you are shown a consent message before any advertising or analytics cookie that requires consent is set. You can accept, reject, or configure your choices there.
You can change or withdraw your consent at any time by reopening that message through the privacy settings link it provides.

sections.title: Other services the site relies on
paragraphs: Two further parties necessarily see your request in the ordinary course of serving the page.
items: jsDelivr — the public CDN that delivers Prettier and its plugins to your browser each time you pick a version. It receives your IP address as part of that request, as any web request would.
Railway — the hosting provider that serves the site. It processes standard web-server request data such as IP address and user agent in order to deliver the page to you.

sections.title: Your rights and choices
paragraphs: Because the site does not collect or store personal information on a server, there is generally no account or record for us to look up, export, or delete.

For the data Google processes through advertising and analytics, Google acts as its own controller. Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access, correct, delete, or restrict the processing of that data, to object to it, or to withdraw your consent. Google's own privacy policy explains how to exercise those rights.
You can also, at any time, clear this site's local storage, block cookies, or use an ad blocker. The tool will keep working.

sections.title: Children
paragraphs: This site is a developer tool and is not directed at children. We do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone under the age of 16.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: We may update this policy as the site changes or as advertising and privacy requirements evolve. The date shown at the top of this page always reflects the most recent revision.
